transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-08 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus C. (Redwood SE on at start), Marcus L. (Fitstone CTO), Sofia (PM), Devon (ML Eng)

Summary: exploratory discovery to align on per-token pricing sensitivity, batching and KV cache levers, and what hosting fit (hosted/dedicated/private) makes sense given Fitstone's latency SLOs and budget constraints. Customer to provide traffic histogram; Redwood to send pricing + pilot plan.

Topics: budget constraints, latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and cache opportunities, security/residency questions (KMS, SOC2), pilot scope, benchmarks to run.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: okay everyone good to go? um yep, thanks for setting time. uh I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE, and priya's our solutions engineer so she'll jump into the perf bits.
00:08 Sofia: hi thanks, yeah we have about 45 minutes. quick context: Fitstone is building an on-demand clinical summarization feature, so token volumes are spiky and sequence lengths vary a lot. main question is which hosting mix keeps latency under 350ms p95 while not blowing our monthly budget.
00:23 Marcus L: yep and we're sensitive to PHI residency and KMS integration.
00:27 Priya: noted, we'll cover residency and KMS later. first tho, i'd like to sketch how per-token cost maps to batching and cache. is that ok?
00:33 Sofia: absolutely.
00:35 Priya: cool. so at a high level, Redwood hosted per-token price is competitive for steady traffic, but spiky workloads often benefit from dedicated pools or private because you get reserved throughput and can tune batch sizes without noisy neighbor effect. that said, dedicated != always cheaper, depends on utilization.
00:50 Devon: just to be clear, when you say per-token pricing are we talking input+output tokens or just output?
00:55 Jordan: usually it's total tokens (input + output) on the hosted plan. for dedicated we do a blended rate in the reserved contract based on expected throughput — we can model both.
01:03 Priya: also important is KV cache / prefix caching. for summarization if you can cache patient-chart prefixes or templates, your average generation length drops, which reduces tokens and cost. even a small hit-rate on the KV cache reduces per-request cost a lot.
01:18 Marcus L: our summaries often re-use the same system prompt and some ontology, so that seems promising. are there numbers you can share for typical hit-rate savings?
01:26 Priya: rough ballpark: with a 30% effective cache hit on prefixes you can see 15-25% token cost reduction end-to-end, assuming output length unchanged. with batching improvements you can get additional amortization of fixed token overhead.
01:40 Sofia: ok, we need concrete modeling. our budget target is $25k per month for this feature initially.
01:46 Jordan: good to know. can you share expected monthly requests and avg tokens per request?
01:50 Sofia: right now we can give you a 2-week histogram; typical weekday peak is about 40 requests/min for the service zone, median seq len ~600 tokens, 95th ~2800.
02:02 Priya: that's helpful. with 40 rps peaks and those lengths, hosted will be fine for sporadic traffic but the p95 latency target under 350ms is tricky with hosted unless you accept higher cost or use model variants. dedicated lets you configure lower tail latency SLOs.
02:18 Marcus C (Redwood SE): small note — model selection matters too. some quantized variants reduce cost but add a few ms; others are faster but cost more tokens because they require longer prompts. there's tradeoffs all round.
02:31 Devon: we do have infrequent but predictable overnight batch runs too, generating thousands of summaries at lower latency constraints. can Redwood schedule burst capacity or are we forced into full reservation?
02:40 Jordan: Redwood supports burst capacity on dedicated and hosted; dedicated reserved pools can be configured with burst buckets. private on-prem obviously you control all capacity but ops burden is higher.
02:49 Sofia: security — SOC2, SSO, and KMS are mandatory. we also need audit logs for model payloads.
02:56 Priya: we are SOC2 Type II, support SAML/SSO with SCIM for provisioning, and KMS integrations — HSM options for private as well. audit logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM, retention configurable.
03:08 Marcus L: residency — PHI must be stored in our AWS VPC region, is that doable with Redwood Private?
03:13 Jordan: yes, Redwood Private (VPC) can run in your region and we offer on-prem options; the private control plane gives you data residency and optional air-gap installs.
03:21 Sofia: great.
03:23 Priya: back to economics — we'll send a pricing model spreadsheet that models three scenarios: hosted steady-state, dedicated moderate-utilization (commit + burst), and private upfront + ops. that will show per-token effective cost and required utilization break-even points.
03:36 Jordan: for the POC we usually start with hosted + KV cache + adaptive batching to prove the quality and cost. if the observed utilization justifies it we move to dedicated. usually the customer sets a budget ceiling and we run a 4-week pilot with guardrails.
03:49 Devon: what's adaptive batching? does that introduce latency spikes while it accumulates tokens?
03:54 Priya: adaptive batching tries to collect requests up to a latency cap; our runtime can target a latency SLO (e.g., 50ms tail) and will flush batches earlier if needed. it's workload-aware so for spiky small requests it behaves like single-request, for stable high throughput it batches more aggressively to save cost.
04:12 Marcus C: and prefix/KV caches are consulted first, reducing sequence lengths for cached prefixes which also reduces batch sizes and kv lookup time is tiny compared with generation.
04:21 Sofia: any caveats around hallucination when using quantized models or cache?
04:26 Priya: cache itself doesn't change model outputs except for saving tokens; quantization can slightly change output fidelity. we recommend quality evals and model comparison tests; Redwood Optimize can run regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
04:38 Jordan: quick question — do you need the pilot to include throughput testing at peak? or is quality first?
04:43 Marcus L: both, but quality is gating. we can't degrade clinical summaries. assume we need a set of golden prompts for regressions.
04:50 Priya: noted, we'll include a QA/regression harness.
04:52 Jordan: a couple of competitive questions — you mentioned Anthropic earlier; any reason you're leaning there?
04:56 Sofia: our data-science team has prototypeed on Claude because of conversational strengths but economics at scale are unclear. we want to test multiple model flavors.
05:04 Jordan: fair. Redwood supports switching model variants and automated fallback. we can route low-cost requests to cheaper quantized variants and fall back when quality drops.
05:13 Sofia: ok. next steps?
05:15 Jordan: we'll send pricing spreadsheet and pilot scope by Monday (2026-05-10). Priya will run a quick KV-cache sensitivity run if you share a small sample prompt set, and Devon will export token histograms. then we reconvene for POC scoping w/infra and security.
05:28 Marcus L: timeline sounds good. one more: for dedicated, do you have SLAs for p95 latency?
05:33 Priya: yes for Dedicated we publish latency SLOs and will work with your SRE to set reasonable expectations; exact numbers depend on model and GPU class. we'll include sample perf profiles in the spreadsheet.
05:44 Devon: for private deployment, how long to onboard? we're not looking to do on-prem until later but timeline helps planning.
05:49 Jordan: private VPC deploys typically 6-10 weeks with standard integrations; on-prem air-gap longer, depends on IT cycles. we'll put rough timelines in the doc.
05:59 Sofia: perfect.
06:01 Jordan: any blockers on our side?
06:03 Marcus L: none immediate. need to sync legal on DPA and PHI addendum but that's standard.
06:09 Jordan: ok, we'll attach the security pack and sample DPA.
06:12 Priya: i'll note two quick experiments: 1) KV-match rate sensitivity on a 1k-sample, 2) batching latency vs cost curve with your histogram. both should give early signals for host vs dedicated choice.
06:24 Sofia: love that.
06:26 Jordan: recap of action items — Jordan send pricing+pilot scope; Priya run tests; Devon export histograms; customer review security pack; schedule follow-up.
06:36 Marcus L: thanks all.
06:38 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and drop links to the deck and spreadsheet.

End of transcript.
